title: Compact change receipt UX - PRD sketch
content:
Purpose
This is a lightweight PRD sketch describing a compact change receipt concept for customer-managed networking changes in Private deployments. Goal is to define a UX-forward artifact that operators and customers can attach to a network change, providing a terse machine- and human-readable proof that includes who approved, what was changed at a high level, a tamper-evident digest, and pointers to richer telemetry for forensic follow-up.

Why we need it (problem statement)
- Support low-latency approvals and fastish operator workflows while preserving a minimal audit surface for compliance teams.
- Avoid huge audit blobs for every minor network tweak while still enabling reconstruction of events during incident or compliance review.
- Give customers a portable, vendor-agnostic compact receipt that they can store in their own evidence store (or forward to SIEM).

Primary goals
1) Define the schema and UX for a compact change receipt that:
   - Is ~1–5 KB when serialized (target)
   - Encodes a digest of the change and minimal metadata
   - Contains approval pointers (who, policy-id, small signature or approval token)
   - Includes stable references to richer telemetry (pre/post snapshots, packet captures, logged events) that can be retrieved if needed
2) Design the operator-facing UX for creating and consuming receipts:
   - Single-click “issue receipt” in the operator console when applying a change
   - API endpoint for receipt issuance for integrations and automation
3) Define retention and lifecycle recommendations: ephemeral in control plane caches, customer-owned immutable copy recommended for compliance archives.

Non-goals
- Not intended to replace full forensic archives or SIEM feeds.
- Not a cryptographic notarization service (no external notary by default), although receipts should support optional integration with customer KMS/HSM or external signing services.

Stakeholders
- Product: owns UX and policy mapping
- Infra/Runtime: ensures receipt generation on change application and attaches runtime digests
- SRE/Observability: wires telemetry references and ensures snapshot hooks exist
- Security/Compliance: approves schema and retention defaults

Personas and user stories
- Platform operator: "I applied a small routing policy update and need a concise proof that I followed the agreed change window and approvals, so I can link it to the incident ticket later."
- Customer security lead: "I want a compact artifact that my SIEM can ingest quickly and that points back to fuller evidence if I need to investigate."
- Auditor: "I need to verify that the change was authorized and that the recorded digest matches the archived detailed snapshot."

Proposed compact receipt shape (high-level fields for UX)
- receipt_id: short stable UUID-like string for quick reference
- timestamp_utc: ISO-8601
- actor: human-readable name or service account (low entropy)
- change_type: enum (route, firewall, nat, config, keystore, operator-script)
- scope: short path (tenant-id / edge-id / vpc-id)
- summary: 1–2 sentence human summary entered by operator or auto-generated
- digest: base64url or hex of a canonicalized digest over the detailed change bundle (tight spec below)
- delta_digest: optional digest of the user-visible delta (helpful for quick comparisons)
- approval_tokens: small list of {approver, policy_id, token_reference} — tokens are short opaque ids the control-plane can verify later
- evidence_refs: list of stable URIs to richer telemetry (e.g., s3://…/snapshots/abc or internal://trace/12345) — these are only pointers, not embedded data
- retention_hint: short tag indicating recommended retention class (ephemeral, short-term, archive)
- signature_meta: optional small map for signing metadata (which key id signed it, algorithm, signature ref) — we keep this shallow to preserve compactness

Important UX constraints
- Keep free-form fields short (summary max 280 chars).
- Display a compact receipt card in the Console change history with: receipt_id, timestamp, actor, change_type, small status badge (approved / auto-approved / manual-escrow), link to evidence, and quick-verify action button.
- Console quick-verify triggers a 1-step remote integrity check: fetch the referenced snapshot digest and compare with receipt.digest. For performance, we should do a sampled verify by default and full verify on demand.

Canonicalization and digest rules (operator-focused)
- Define a stable canonicalization algorithm for the change bundle: deterministic key ordering, minimal whitespace, stable timestamp normalization.
- Target digest algorithm: SHA-256 hex -> base16 string. Keep output length predictable.
- delta_digest is computed only over a normalized delta representation (fields changed).

Approval flow integration points
- API: POST /v1/receipts -> 201 + receipt body. Called by control-plane after change application and approval evaluation.
- Web: Console will surface a pre-issued "pending receipt" while waiting for approvals; on final application the receipt is emitted.
- Automation: automation tools (Terraform, CI/CD pipelines) can request ephemeral approval tokens to be embedded in approval_tokens for receipt issuance. Tokens should expire quickly and be single-use.

Retention and compliance recommendations
- Default retention_hint for minor operational changes: short-term (30 days).
- For changes that touch keystore/certs or escalate privileges: archive (recommended 7 years or per customer policy).
- Allow customers to configure automatic export hooks that deposit receipts into their cloud storage or into a supplied SIEM connector.

Edge cases and questions to resolve
- How do we represent rolled-back changes or partial failures? Proposal: issue a new receipt referencing prior receipt_id with an action=rollback tag and link to the failure trace.
- What if referenced evidence is deleted? Receipt must remain valid; on verify we return evidence-missing state and rely on digest for tamper evidence.
- For air-gapped / private deployments: provide an offline issuance mode that returns a compact signed blob the customer can upload later.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- API: create/GET receipt endpoints implemented in control plane for Private deployments.
- Console: display receipt card in change history and surface evidence links.
- Runtime: emission of digest for any network change and ability to store snapshot pointer.
- Docs: canonicalization and digest rules published; integration guide for SIEM export.

Next steps and milestones (rough)
- Week 1: finalize schema draft with Security and Runtime (this doc).
- Week 2–3: implement emission hooks and produce receipts for a narrow set of change types (route, firewall).
- Week 4: Console card + simple verify action.
- Week 5–6: SIEM export hookup + retention config.

Open design notes / discussion prompts (for product review)
- UX tradeoff: show full approval details inline vs. require a click to reveal — recommendation: collapsed by default, expand for details.
- Security: should we require signed receipts for compliance customers by default? Ops cost vs. compliance ROI.
- Integration: offer a small reference lambda that consumes receipts and writes to common SIEM formats (CEF, JSON).

Appendix: example compact receipt (illustrative; serialized JSON would be compacted/minified in practice)
{\n  "receipt_id": "rcpt-45b9e7",\n  "timestamp_utc": "2026-01-20T15:04:12Z",\n  "actor": "ops-jane@redwood-corp",\n  "change_type": "firewall",\n  "scope": "tenant:acme-corp/vpc:west-1-edge-42",\n  "summary": "Opened port 5432 for analytics-job-window",\n  "digest": "b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184f0a1f…",\n  "delta_digest": "ef797c8118f02dfb6490f…",\n  "approval_tokens": ["tok-9a7f", "tok-3c2b"],\n  "evidence_refs": ["internal://snapshots/2026-01-20/edge-42/pre", "s3://acme-archives/change/rcpt-45b9e7/details.json"],\n  "retention_hint": "short-term",\n  "signature_meta": {"key_id": "kp-03", "algo": "rsa-sha256", "signature_ref": "internal://sign/rcpt-45b9e7.sig"}\n}

(End of sketch)

Notes to reviewers: please comment inline on the canonicalization rules and the minimal fields you think are required for your compliance needs. If you want a version that uses a stronger signing model (cert chains + timestamping), say so and include expected threat model details.
